A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian Loss Smoothing study despite the changed title. All 16 pages of v2 and 21 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations and appendices A–E, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original certified-training experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10, including accuracy comparisons, loss-landscape measurements and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds results for TinyImageNet, additional network configurations, α-CROWN training and initialization comparisons.

M1.justification: The PGPE and RGS algorithms already appear in v2 and retain their core procedures. v3 adds a concrete α-CROWN-PGPE variant incorporating inner ReLU-slope optimization into bound computation, extending the implemented training approach beyond the previous relaxations.

E1.justification: v3 adds certified classification on TinyImageNet at epsilon-infinity 1/255, extending evaluation to a more demanding dataset with 64-by-64 inputs. MNIST, CIFAR-10 and their previously evaluated perturbation radii remain covered.

E2.justification: v3 removes the PGD comparator rows from Table 1. Its expanded main comparison adds TAPS on CNN7 for MNIST and MTL-IBP on CNN7 for CIFAR-10; Appendix D.1 also adds MTL-IBP to the retained large-perturbation CNN5 comparisons. These changes substantially strengthen the reference comparisons beyond the original larger-network IBP baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix E changes the stated standard-training learning rate from 5e-4 to 5e-5. RGS switches from its separate 60/80-epoch MNIST/CIFAR-10 schedules to the standard 70/160-epoch schedules. v3 also introduces CNN3-tiny, CNN5-L and IBP-initialized RGS controls. These are reported protocol changes; they do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds an initialization analysis testing whether IBP-trained starting weights help RGS at large perturbations, and a direct PGPE-versus-RGS analysis across CNN3-tiny, CNN3 and datasets. These address previously unexplored explanations for performance differences. The existing population-size, smoothing-scale and loss-landscape ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions show confidence bands for the same loss-landscape estimates using 128 samples, in v2 Figure 5 and v3 Figure 4. Neither introduces repeated-training-run counts, seed-based accuracy uncertainty or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for α-CROWN, TinyImageNet, wider networks and supplementary comparisons. Reported CNN5 DP-RGS certified accuracy changes from 97.56% to 97.15% on MNIST and from 54.83% to 54.91% on CIFAR-10. Because the stated RGS protocols also change, these are revised results rather than demonstrated same-setting gains or losses. Retained Table 1 relaxation scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the earlier beta-smoothness formulation with Theorem 3.1, adding bounded-domain Lipschitz guarantees, a formal definition of local sharpness and a sharpness-reduction lemma. Appendix B.1 supplies substantially expanded arguments. The minima-alignment discussion and RGS discontinuity counterexamples in B.2–B.3 remain.

C1.justification: v3 qualifies the earlier 'overcoming the paradox' framing as mitigating known factors and taking a step toward overcoming it. Headline performance claims are restricted to many settings, with small perturbations emphasized in the evaluation. The central GLS, PGPE and RGS contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking large-perturbation difficulties to IBP regularization and unstable neurons, and PGPE/RGS differences to parameter-space size and convergence. The discussion now acknowledges potentially unidentified causes of the paradox and continuing CNN7 scaling limits. RGS's discontinuity limitations were already present in v2.

D1.justification: v3 documents α-CROWN slope optimization, additional architectures, initialization choices, TinyImageNet preprocessing, dataset splits and A100 resource use. It expands training-cost reporting and adds baseline training times. Disclosure is not uniformly improved: v2's explicit RGS batch sizes disappear when v3 refers RGS settings to standard training.

R1.justification: v3 adds Lee et al. (2021) to the explanation of training difficulties, Xu et al. (2020) for α-CROWN and Mao et al. (2024) for benchmark positioning, alongside dataset, initialization and application references. Most positioning remains intact. De Palma's 2023-to-2024 citation update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 now introduces the training difficulties and GLS theory before PGPE, replacing the previous PGPE-first narrative. Limitations becomes Discussion, and Appendix D gains separate analytical subsections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains an RGS column, and the main benchmark table is expanded and regrouped by architecture with parameter counts. New tables present α-CROWN, PGPE/RGS comparisons and baseline runtimes. Existing plots are largely retained but resized, relocated or renumbered, alongside broader typography and page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through broader evaluation, initialization controls and clearer applicability limits. However, the new general sharpness guarantee in Theorem 3.1 relies on Lemma B.2, whose proof neglects Gaussian contributions outside a local neighborhood using a small-smoothing approximation without qualifying the theorem accordingly. This central rigor concern coexists with clear empirical and reporting gains, leaving their net effect on overall quality uncertain.
